# QgsGeometry.buffer

## Syntax
buffer(self, distance: float, segments: int, feedback: QgsFeedback | None = None) -> QgsGeometry

## Description
Returns a buffer region around this geometry having the given width and with a specified number of segments used to approximate curves. The optional feedback argument allows for early cancellation (since QGIS 4.2). buffer(self, distance: float, segments: int, endCapStyle: Qgis.EndCapStyle, joinStyle: Qgis.JoinStyle, miterLimit: float, feedback: Optional[QgsFeedback] = None) -> QgsGeometry Returns a buffer region around the geometry, with additional style options.

```python
from qgis.core import QgsGeometry
result = QgsGeometry.buffer(distance, segments, feedback)
```

# QgsGeometry.intersection

## Syntax
intersection(self, geometry: QgsGeometry, parameters: QgsGeometryParameters = QgsGeometryParameters(), feedback: QgsFeedback | None = None) -> QgsGeometry

## Description
Returns a geometry representing the points shared by this geometry and other. If the input is a NULL geometry, the output will also be a NULL geometry. If an error was encountered while creating the result, more information can be retrieved by calling lastError() on the returned geometry. Since QGIS 3.28 the optional parameters argument can be used to specify parameters which control the intersection results.

```python
from qgis.core import QgsGeometry
result = QgsGeometry.intersection(geometry, parameters, feedback)
```

# QgsGeometry.difference

## Syntax
difference(self, geometry: QgsGeometry, parameters: QgsGeometryParameters = QgsGeometryParameters(), feedback: QgsFeedback | None = None) -> QgsGeometry

## Description
Returns a geometry representing the points making up this geometry that do not make up other. If the input is a NULL geometry, the output will also be a NULL geometry. If an error was encountered while creating the result, more information can be retrieved by calling lastError() on the returned geometry. Since QGIS 3.28 the optional parameters argument can be used to specify parameters which control the difference results.

```python
from qgis.core import QgsGeometry
result = QgsGeometry.difference(geometry, parameters, feedback)
```

# QgsGeometry.simplify

## Syntax
simplify(self, tolerance: float, feedback: QgsFeedback | None = None) -> QgsGeometry

## Description
Returns a simplified version of this geometry using a specified tolerance value. The optional feedback argument allows for early cancellation (since QGIS 4.2).

```python
from qgis.core import QgsGeometry
result = QgsGeometry.simplify(tolerance, feedback)
```

# QgsGeometry.centroid

## Syntax
centroid(self) -> QgsGeometry

## Description
Returns the center of mass of a geometry. If the input is a NULL geometry, the output will also be a NULL geometry. If an error was encountered while creating the result, more information can be retrieved by calling lastError() on the returned geometry. for line based geometries, the center point of the line is returned, and for point based geometries, the point itself is returned

```python
from qgis.core import QgsGeometry
result = QgsGeometry.centroid()
```


# QgsGeometry.makeValid

## Syntax
makeValid(self, method: Qgis.MakeValidMethod = Qgis.MakeValidMethod.Linework, keepCollapsed: bool = False, feedback: QgsFeedback | None = None) -> QgsGeometry

## Description
Attempts to make an invalid geometry valid without losing vertices. Already-valid geometries are returned without further intervention. In case of full or partial dimensional collapses, the output geometry may be a collection of lower-to-equal dimension geometries or a geometry of lower dimension. Single polygons may become multi-geometries in case of self-intersections. It preserves Z values, but M values will be dropped.

```python
from qgis.core import QgsGeometry
result = QgsGeometry.makeValid(method, keepCollapsed, feedback)
```
